input_latex: u_t = 1\,u_{xx},\qquad 0 < x < 1;\quad u(0,t) = 0,\quad u(L,t) = 0;\quad u(x,0) = x \left(1 - x\right)
normal_latex: u_t = 1\,u_{xx},\qquad 0 < x < 1;\quad u(0,t) = 0,\quad u(L,t) = 0;\quad u(x,0) = x \left(1 - x\right)
summary: Heat equation on a rod of length L. Both ends held at 0. Use the slider on the graph to watch the temperature evolve.

methods.name: Separation of variables
methods.reason: The equation and boundary conditions are linear and homogeneous, so product solutions can be superposed.

steps.title: Separate the variables
steps.text: Look for solutions that are a product of a function of each variable. Substituting and dividing by the product puts each variable on its own side, so both sides equal a constant, written \(-\lambda\).

steps.title: Solve the eigenvalue problem
steps.text: The boundary conditions apply to the spatial factor. Only \(\lambda > 0\) gives non-zero solutions, and they are sines.

steps.title: Solve the time equation
steps.text: Each \(\lambda_n\) gives a time factor that decays; the higher modes die out fastest.
latex: T' + k\lambda_n T = 0 \quad\Rightarrow\quad T_n = e^{-k\lambda_n t}

steps.title: Superpose
steps.text: The equation and boundary conditions are linear and homogeneous, so any sum of these products is also a solution.

steps.title: Find the coefficients
steps.text: Setting \(t = 0\) must give \(f(x)\). The coefficients are the expansion coefficients of the data in the eigenfunctions, found with their orthogonality.

steps.title: Long-time behaviour
steps.text: Every term decays, so the temperature tends to 0 everywhere.

steps.title: Solution
latex: u(x,t) \approx 0.25801\,e^{- \pi^{2} t}\,\sin{\left(\pi x \right)} + 0.009556\,e^{- 9 \pi^{2} t}\,\sin{\left(3 \pi x \right)} + 0.0020641\,e^{- 25 \pi^{2} t}\,\sin{\left(5 \pi x \right)} + \cdots

steps.title: Check
steps.text: Checked numerically: the series satisfies the equation at sample points and the boundary conditions. With 20 terms it reproduces the initial temperature closely.
